_comment: Baseline for the Pulse formula property checks. Two kinds of number, judged differently.
violations: matched EXACTLY and in BOTH directions. A count that rises is a regression;
a count that falls is a deliberate semantic change whose baseline must move in the same
commit as the change. The normtest entries are real, triaged residuals, not noise:
simplify_shallow is shallow by contract so non-idempotence is its expected shape and the
caller iterates, and the Atom.eval entries are the `x mod 1` family, which the Phi layer
absorbs end to end (x % 1 < 0 is correctly pruned by the full solver). They are pinned so
that a change to either is noticed rather than tolerated.
reach_floors: a property that never reaches its condition reports a pass for the wrong
reason. These harnesses have produced four such false clean runs, so the floors are part
of the verdict. They sit well below the observed values at the pinned seed, because they
exist to catch a property going dead, not to track small movements.
Observed at seed 20261116, pre-push sizes (20000/40000/30000), on the engine as of the
PER TIER, because violation counts are matched exactly and scale with the iteration
count. The nightly sizes are ten times the pre-push ones and reach one shape the
smaller run never does (B2 Sat-then-UNSAT), so a single shared baseline would fail
